by: Claude Code (opus), titles and abstracts only

question.population: Adults who had bowel polyps (colorectal adenomas) removed, or adults in general
question.outcome: Colorectal adenomas (bowel polyps), new or coming back

decisions.reason: Pools observational studies of calcium intake, not randomised trials, and the outcome is colorectal cancer rather than adenomas.
Pools placebo-controlled RCTs of calcium supplements; outcome is colorectal adenoma recurrence.
Pools RCTs of calcium supplements in patients with a history of adenomas; outcome is adenoma recurrence.
Pools prospective observational studies of calcium intake, not randomised trials of supplements against placebo.
Pools double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs of calcium in people with previous adenomas; outcome is adenoma recurrence.
Pools RCTs of calcium versus placebo in people with removed adenomas; outcome is adenoma recurrence.
Pools placebo-controlled RCTs of calcium in people with previous adenomas; outcome is adenoma recurrence.
Includes a meta-analysis of calcium versus placebo RCTs in people with a history of adenomas; outcome is adenoma recurrence.
Pools placebo-controlled RCTs of calcium in people with previous adenomas; outcome is adenoma recurrence.

question.intervention: Calcium supplements, alone or with vitamin D

decisions.reason: Looks at how often stones come back in people who already form calcium stones, across many treatments; calcium supplements against placebo are not tested.
Calcium supplements and new kidney stones match, but it covers only postmenopausal women and is a narrative review of trials and observational data.
Covers diet, fluids and unnamed supplements to prevent repeat stones in stone formers; calcium appears only as part of mixed diets, not as a supplement.
Calcium supplements and kidney stone outcomes match, but only in people with osteoporosis, sometimes with other drugs, and it includes cohort studies.

question.outcome: Pre-eclampsia or high blood pressure in pregnancy

decisions.reason: Pooled RCTs of calcium versus placebo in pregnant women, with pre-eclampsia as the critical outcome.
Calcium vs placebo for pre-eclampsia, but supplements started before pregnancy in non-pregnant women who had pre-eclampsia before.
Pooled RCTs of calcium versus control in pregnant women, reporting pre-eclampsia and pregnancy-induced hypertension.
Calcium in pregnancy, but this review explicitly excludes hypertension outcomes and looks at preterm birth and birthweight.
Network meta-analysis of RCTs that includes calcium versus placebo in pregnancy for preventing pre-eclampsia.
Meta-analysis of RCTs of calcium supplementation for pre-eclampsia prevention in women before or during pregnancy.
Calcium for primary hypertension in normotensive people in general, not in pregnancy.
Calcium given with aspirin and compared with aspirin alone, in high-risk pregnant women, for pre-eclampsia.
Calcium for primary hypertension in normotensive people in general, not in pregnancy.
Pooled RCTs of calcium versus placebo in pregnant women for pre-eclampsia and gestational hypertension.
Has a calcium subgroup for pre-eclampsia, but only in high-risk women, and some started before conception.
Calcium plus vitamin D for blood pressure in general populations, not pregnancy.
Calcium vs placebo for pre-eclampsia, but started before or early in pregnancy, in women with previous pre-eclampsia.
Pooled RCTs of calcium supplements in pregnant women for pre-eclampsia and gestational hypertension.
Pooled RCTs of calcium versus placebo in pregnancy, reporting high blood pressure and pre-eclampsia.
Its only included trial gave calcium together with antioxidants and other supplements, starting in early pregnancy.
Calcium plus vitamin D for blood pressure in adults in general, not pregnancy.
Direct meta-analysis of RCTs of calcium versus placebo in pregnancy for pre-eclampsia.
Calcium for primary hypertension in normotensive people in general, not in pregnancy.
Pooled multicentre RCTs of calcium in pregnancy for hypertension and pre-eclampsia.
Pregnant women given calcium vs placebo/no treatment, but the review explicitly excludes hypertension outcomes and looks at preterm birth and birthweight.
Meta-analysis of RCTs of calcium vs placebo in pregnancy for preventing pre-eclampsia.
Pregnant women given calcium vs placebo/no treatment, but outcomes other than hypertension (preterm birth, birthweight) are the focus.
RCTs of calcium vs placebo or no calcium in pregnancy, with pooled pre-eclampsia and high blood pressure outcomes.
Outcome is blood pressure in the offspring, not maternal pre-eclampsia, and it includes observational studies.
Calcium and blood pressure in non-pregnant people only.
RCTs of at least 1 g/day calcium vs placebo in pregnancy, with pooled high blood pressure and pre-eclampsia outcomes.
Low-dose calcium in pregnancy for pre-eclampsia; a separate pooled subgroup of calcium alone matches, though co-supplement and quasi-randomised trials are also included.
Treats primary hypertension in non-pregnant adults; pregnant women were excluded.
RCTs of calcium in pregnancy for gestational hypertension and pre-eclampsia, but limited to women in developing countries.
RCTs of at least 1 g/day calcium vs placebo in pregnancy, with pooled high blood pressure and pre-eclampsia outcomes.
Systematic review of RCTs of at least 1 g/day calcium vs placebo in pregnancy, with pooled pre-eclampsia risk.
Combined mineral supplements for primary hypertension in non-pregnant adults.
RCTs of at least 1 g/day calcium vs placebo in pregnancy, with pooled high blood pressure and pre-eclampsia outcomes.
RCTs of at least 1 g/day calcium vs placebo in pregnancy, with pooled high blood pressure and pre-eclampsia outcomes.
RCTs of at least 1 g/day calcium vs placebo in pregnancy, with pooled high blood pressure and pre-eclampsia outcomes.
Calcium and blood pressure in general normotensive and hypertensive persons, not pregnant women.
Epidemiologic review of calcium and blood pressure that excludes trials in pregnant women.
Calcium vs placebo and blood pressure in general populations, not pregnancy or pre-eclampsia.
Calcium and blood pressure in hypertensive or normotensive people generally, not pregnancy outcomes.
Pooled 14 randomised trials of calcium supplements versus control in pregnant women, reporting blood pressure and pre-eclampsia.

question.population: Adults in general or older adults (not a group defined by one illness, such as people in intensive care, on dialysis or with cancer)
question.intervention: Calcium supplements, alone or with vitamin D
question.outcome: Heart attacks, strokes or other cardiovascular events

decisions.reason: Pooled RCTs of calcium alone or with vitamin D and reported heart attack, stroke and cardiovascular death outcomes.
Pooled double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs of calcium supplements for CVD and coronary heart disease outcomes.
Pooled RCTs of calcium supplements, with or without vitamin D, for coronary heart disease and heart attack, alongside cohort studies.
RCTs of calcium or calcium plus vitamin D against placebo in generally healthy adults, looking at CVD events.
Umbrella review that includes a meta-analysis of calcium plus vitamin D RCTs for stroke and cardiovascular outcomes in adults.
Meta-analysis of supplement RCTs, including calcium, for cardiovascular outcomes.
Pooled studies of vitamin D or calcium, alone or combined, for heart attack and other cardiovascular events in community-dwelling adults.
RCTs of mineral supplements in healthy adults for CVD prevention; calcium falls under the minerals reviewed, though the abstract doesn't name it.
Narrative review that summarises earlier meta-analyses; it doesn't do its own pooling of randomised trials.
Pooled RCTs of calcium with or without vitamin D against placebo or no treatment for coronary heart disease, but only in elderly women.
Narrative review that discusses an earlier meta-analysis; it doesn't do its own pooling of randomised trials.
Meta-analysis of placebo-controlled RCTs of calcium supplements in adults over 40, looking at heart attack and stroke.
Pooled RCTs of calcium, alone or with vitamin D, against placebo for cardiovascular events in adults.
Meta-analysis of placebo-controlled trials of calcium with or without vitamin D for heart attack and stroke.
Looks at supplements given alongside cardiovascular drugs, not calcium compared with placebo for cardiovascular events.
Reviewed trials of supplements, including calcium, for primary prevention of CVD in community-dwelling adults.

question.population: Adults over 50, mostly women after menopause (not a group defined by one illness)
question.intervention: Calcium supplements, alone or with vitamin D

decisions.reason: Pools RCTs of calcium alone and calcium plus vitamin D vs placebo or no treatment for fractures in adults, a broader group that includes older people.
Calcium plus vitamin D RCTs pooled for fractures, but only in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, a group defined by one illness.
Pools RCTs of calcium, vitamin D or both vs placebo or no treatment for fractures in adults over 60.
Pools RCTs of daily vitamin D3 plus calcium for hip fracture prevention in adults over 65.
Pools RCTs of calcium plus vitamin D vs control for fractures, but in older people with osteoporosis, including treatment.
Postmenopausal women and fracture outcome match, but focus is mainly vitamin D and bone markers, and trials were not pooled.
Pools RCTs of calcium supplements with or without vitamin D for fractures in people over 50.
Pools RCTs of calcium, vitamin D or both vs placebo or no treatment for fractures in community-dwelling adults over 50.
Includes a pooled analysis of RCTs of vitamin D plus calcium vs control for any and hip fracture.
Network meta-analysis of RCTs of calcium, vitamin D or both vs placebo or no treatment for fractures in older adults.
Reviews RCTs of calcium alone or with vitamin D vs placebo for fractures in community-dwelling adults 50 and older.
Pools RCTs of calcium plus vitamin D for total and hip fractures in middle-aged to older adults.
Pools RCTs of calcium supplements vs placebo for hip and nonvertebral fractures, mainly in postmenopausal women.
Calcium supplements for fractures in postmenopausal women, but only observational data were pooled; the 4 RCTs were not.
Meta-analysis of observational studies of dietary calcium, not randomised trials of calcium supplements.
Methods study comparing overlapping meta-analyses of vitamin D, not a pooled analysis answering the question.
Meta-regression of whether bone density change predicts fracture reduction, not the effect of calcium vs placebo on fractures.
Pools RCTs of vitamin D plus calcium for fractures in older adults, mostly postmenopausal women.
Pools RCTs of calcium alone or with vitamin D for fractures in people aged 50 and older.
Pools RCTs of vitamin D plus calcium vs placebo or no treatment for hip fracture in postmenopausal women and older men.

question.population: Adults over 50 (not a group defined by one illness)
question.intervention: Calcium supplements or more calcium in the diet

decisions.reason: Both arms got calcium/vitamin D; the review tests adding exercise, not calcium versus placebo.
BMD outcome matches, but calcium is always given with vitamin D, and only to postmenopausal women who already have osteoporosis.
Compares herbal medicine plus supplements with supplements alone in osteoporosis patients, so it tests the herbs, not calcium.
Calcium versus control on BMD, but the population is pregnant women, not adults over 50.
Calcium versus placebo on BMD, but the population is premenopausal women aged roughly 18–42.
Calcium versus placebo or no treatment on BMD, but the population is lactating women, not adults over 50.
Population is people on tenofovir drugs, calcium comes with vitamin D, and cohort studies are included.
Children and adolescents, and calcium is combined with a physical activity intervention.
BMD outcome matches, but calcium is only given together with vitamin K and the age group is not specified.
Pooled RCTs of calcium from diet or supplements in people over 50, measuring BMD.
Pooled trials of calcium versus placebo or no treatment in postmenopausal women aged 50–83, measuring spine BMD.
Tests probiotics, prebiotics or synbiotics, not calcium.
Calcium with or without vitamin D versus control on BMD, but in healthy males of all ages rather than adults over 50.
Pooled RCTs of calcium versus placebo or usual diet in postmenopausal women, measuring BMD.
Withdrawn version of the review above: same calcium-versus-placebo trials in postmenopausal women, measuring BMD.
Calcium versus placebo on BMD, but the population is healthy children.
Tests vitamin D supplements without calcium.
Pooled RCTs of calcium versus placebo or usual diet in postmenopausal women, measuring BMD.
Meta-regression asks whether BMD changes predict fracture risk, not whether calcium changes BMD.
Calcium versus placebo on BMD, but the population is healthy children.
Compares ossein-hydroxyapatite with calcium carbonate, so the comparator is another active calcium product rather than placebo or no treatment.
Pools randomised trials of calcium, with or without vitamin D, in adults aged 50 or older, with percentage change in bone mineral density as an outcome.
Covers adults aged 18 to 50, mostly in cross-sectional studies, so the population falls outside the over-50 group and few trials are included.
